submission.natural_language_explanation: Broad previous-token head: predict ordinary prose active-weak (most sentences cross the line somewhere), with activity on the words that open the object of a verb or preposition (the 'the'/'a'/'their'/'me'/name right after 'told', 'reminded', 'gave', 'on', 'in', 'of', 'to', 'from'), attending to that governing word and fading over the noun phrase, and strongest (up to max) on such a determiner after a speech verb deep in a long passage (', told the Providence Journal'). Predict whole texts inactive only when they are entirely one of these: a bare noun phrase with no preposition ('The tall building.', 'My brother and his friends.'); interjections, discourse words and punctuation ('Yes. No. Maybe.', 'Well, then, and so.'); a two- or three-word intransitive clause ('She smiled.', 'The bell rang.'); or a copular clause 'The N is/was ADJ.' — any verb or preposition followed by its object (e.g. 'Then he told them,') makes a text active.
